extracted_data.title: A reciprocal learning strategy for semisupervised medical image segmentation
extracted_data.architecture: 3D V-Net (teacher-student reciprocal learning, RLSS)
extracted_data.architecture_details: V-Net backbone for both teacher and student; teacher pretrained supervised, student learns from teacher pseudo-labels, teacher optimized via gradient-based feedback signal from student's performance on labeled data (meta-learning style, Eq. 12); adds unsupervised transformation-consistency regularization (rotations 90-deg increments, flips) with Gaussian warm-up weighting; SGD, 6000 iterations, lr 0.01 decayed 0.1 every 2500 iterations; extension of authors' MICCAI 2021 conference paper with new regularization term and breast MRI dataset
extracted_data.loss_function: Cross-entropy: supervised CE (teacher pretraining), CE on pseudo-labels (student), feedback CE loss (teacher), plus CE-based unsupervised consistency regularization with time-dependent Gaussian warm-up lambda(t)
extracted_data.preprocessing: CT soft tissue window [-125, 275] HU; all images normalized to zero mean/unit variance; random subvolume crops (96x96x96 pancreas, 112x112x80 left atrium, 256x96x80 breast); rotation/flip augmentation
extracted_data.postprocessing: Sliding-window whole-volume inference from student network; connected true-positive regions used for distance metrics
datasets: In-house breast DCE-MRI (200 scans, 273 biopsy-proven cancers)
extracted_data.dataset_size: 82 pancreas CT (62 train/20 test), 100 left atrium MR (80/20), 200 breast MRI (68/132); 10/20/30/100% labeled ratios tested
extracted_data.limitations: Failure cases: inaccurate boundaries from isotropic intensity (pancreas), false positives on fat, chest wall, axillary lymph node; requires paired networks; only single-structure tasks evaluated
extracted_data.future_work: Authors state strategy is a general semisupervised solution with potential for other 3D segmentation tasks

extracted_data.title: LobePrior Segments Lung Lobes on Computed Tomography Images in the Presence of Severe Abnormalities
extracted_data.architecture: LobePrior: three-stage pipeline (low-res AttUNet -> high-res multi-decoder AttUNet -> prior-based post-processing)
extracted_data.architecture_details: Stage 1: 3D AttUNet (3D U-Net + spatial attention module from Gorriz et al.) on 128x128x128 downsampled volumes, softmax; Stage 2: 3D AttUNet with shared encoder + 7 decoders, 13 input channels (CT + 5-channel probabilistic prior + 7 Stage-1 masks), 128^3 patches, per-decoder sigmoid; outputs 7 structures (whole lung, 5 lobes, airway); Stage 3: max-activation labeling, largest connected component, gap filling via probabilistic templates (7 groups from 50 registered Tang et al. volumes, SyN diffeomorphic registration via DIPY, composite MSE/NCC/MI template selection); synthetic lesion insertion augmentation with Gaussian-blended edges and HU matching; extends CBEB 2024 conference version (single shared-encoder network replacing 5 independent AttUNets, Dice replaces focal loss)
extracted_data.loss_function: Dice loss (softmax in Stage 1, sigmoid per decoder in Stage 2)
extracted_data.preprocessing: Resample to 1mm isotropic, HU clip [-1024,600], normalize to [0,1]; center-of-mass init + SyN diffeomorphic registration (DIPY, MI metric, multi-resolution pyramid [10000,1000,100], Gaussian smoothing); DICOM->NIfTI, anonymization; 80/20 train/val patient-level disjoint splits
extracted_data.postprocessing: Max sigmoid activation across decoders, whole-lung mask as background indicator, LCC per structure, lobe assignment of unclassified voxels via selected probabilistic template, rigid transform back to original space with interpolation
extracted_data.dataset_size: 771 total volumes: 150 train (50 LUNA16/Tang + 100 in-house), 85 test (LOCCA 60, COVID-19 CT 15, CoronaCases 10)

extracted_data.architecture: JRS-GAN: 3D U-Net-like generator (unsupervised DVF estimation) + PatchGAN discriminator (closed-loop)
extracted_data.architecture_details: Generator: 3D U-Net-like CNN, 3x3x3 convs, LeakyReLU+BN, strided convs/upsampling, reduced output FOV, predicts DVF; NiftyNet resampling layer warps images end-to-end; 96x96x96 patches, 1000/pair within torso mask, warp both directions per iteration. Pipeline: semi-automatic physician reference contours (Aquarius iNtuition, spline-interpolated) -> cardiac ROI -> HU threshold defines fat ground truth; a 2D U-Net (TensorFlow, 1x GTX 970, 250 epochs, Adam, L2-weighted softmax cross-entropy, 256x256 axial inputs, rotation augmentation) trained on 100 scans and tested on 19. s3.exclusion_reason: Triggers exclusion criterion 3 (not truly 3D/volumetric): the paper is explicitly a 2.5D study — 2D axial CT slices (512x512) fed with adjacent-slice 'inter-slice' context channels rather than 3D volumes or 3D convolutions, and the authors themselves frame 3D segmentation as the harder alternative they avoid. Also triggers criterion 7 (application without methodological contribution): '2.5D ResUNet' and '2.5D DenseUNet' are existing building blocks (U-Net + residual blocks / + densely connected blocks) applied to a new dataset, with no novel module, loss, or architecture proposed; the paper's substantive content is a first-hand data-preparation/annotation-cost and domain-shift study (KiTS19 -> 4 Thai patients), and its stated end goal (Bosniak III/IV renal-cyst malignant-potential classification) is explicitly NOT addressed ('the proposed models only deal with the first task... there is no model proposed for Bosniak renal cyst classification yet'). Criteria 1, 4, 5 are met (DL primary, CT, mean kidney Dice >=95% on KiTS19 validation / 87.69% on Thai cohort) and criterion 3-organ is met (kidney parenchyma, not tumor-only), but a single exclusion criterion suffices.
s3.screening_notes: Borderline on two axes, resolved toward exclude. (a) 3D-ness: 2.5D does carry limited inter-slice context, so it is not '2D slices independently' in the strictest reading, but it is not 3D volume processing either, and this review's scope is DL 3D organ segmentation in CT — consistent with prior 2D/slice-wise exclusions rather than with the 3D method includes (FocusNet 3D CNN, DiagNeXt 3D U-Net/ConvNeXt, LK-attention 3D decomposed convs). (b) Novelty: unlike the method-contribution includes, which each propose a named new component plus ablations, this paper contributes dataset engineering and a comparative evaluation of two pre-existing 2.5D UNet variants; closest precedent is the application-only exclusions (pmc13239417, Miron 2020). Secondary scope concern: segmentation is a means to a lesion-classification (Bosniak) endpoint, and only 4 Thai patients / ~70 slices per patient are annotated, with a large reported domain-shift drop (95% -> 87.69%). If the review protocol counts 2.5D as 3D, this record should be re-screened on pages 7-15 for whether the ResUNet/DenseUNet modifications are presented as novel; results tables, loss function, framework/GPU and code availability are beyond the 6 pages supplied.

extracted_data.title: Automatic kidney segmentation using 2.5D ResUNet and 2.5D DenseUNet for malignant potential analysis in complex renal cyst based on CT images
extracted_data.authors: Kittipongdaja P, Siriborvornratanakul T (National Institute of Development Administration, Bangkok, Thailand)
extracted_data.venue: EURASIP Journal on Image and Video Processing, 2022:5 (Open Access)
extracted_data.architecture: 2.5D ResUNet / 2.5D DenseUNet (U-Net based)
extracted_data.architecture_details: Two U-Net variants: ResUNet (residual blocks) and DenseUNet (densely connected blocks), converted to '2.5D' by extracting both intra-slice and inter-slice features from axial CT slices (i.e. neighbouring-slice context supplied alongside 2D slices, 512x512 px, slice thickness 1-5 mm KiTS19 / 2-3 mm Thai data, ~70 kidney-containing slices per patient used). No 3D convolution or full-volume input described in pp.1-6.
extracted_data.preprocessing: CT number -> Hounsfield Unit conversion via HU = rescale_slope * CT_number + rescale_intercept (slope 1.0, intercept -1024.0 for Thai data; KiTS19 already in HU so skipped); HU clipping/windowing to range -73 to +304 (renal organ HU of interest approx +20 to +40) to remove out-of-range values; min-max normalisation of clipped HU to [0.0, 1.0]; image registration skipped (no misalignment in single-phase KiTS19 and Thai venous-phase data); data augmentation with albumentations 0.2.3: horizontal flip (p=0.5), random brightness/contrast (p=0.5), random gamma (p=0.5), grid distortion (p=0.5, border_mode=cv.BORDER_CONSTANT). Only venous-phase contrast CT selected for the Thai domain-shift experiments.
datasets: KiTS19 (public Kidney Tumour Segmentation Challenge 2019, 300 patients: 210 train / 90 test; 60-patient validation set used for reported Dice)

Self-collected Ramathibodi Hospital abdominal CT cohort (retrospective cross-sectional, 200 patients 2007-2019; only 19 Bosniak III/IV; 4 patients with urologist labelme 4.5.1 annotations used for experiments)

extracted_data.title: Large-Kernel Attention for 3D Medical Image Segmentation
extracted_data.architecture: U-Net with large-kernel (LK) attention module
extracted_data.architecture_details: Novel LK attention block combining convolution and self-attention advantages (local contextual information, long-range dependence, channel adaptation). 3D LK convolution decomposed for efficiency: e.g. 21x21x21 -> 5x5x5 depth-wise conv + 7x7x7 depth-wise dilated conv (dilation 3,3,3) + 1x1x1 conv. Block flow: group normalization + ReLU -> decomposed LK convolution -> sigmoid -> attention map, multiplied elementwise with the feature map and summed to produce output. Integrated into U-Net; comprehensive ablations on decomposition feasibility and on module placement/deployment, with Mid-type LK attention-based U-Net reported as best.

extracted_data.title: Towards Synergistic Deep Learning Models for Volumetric Cirrhotic Liver Segmentation in MRIs
extracted_data.architecture: nnSynergyNet3D (auto-configured cascaded 3D U-Net with synergistic continuous+discrete latent spaces)
extracted_data.architecture_details: Two-stage 3D cascade: low-resolution 3D U-Net refines predictions of a high-resolution 3D U-Net. Bottleneck holds two complementary latent spaces — F1 (continuous, fine-grained) and F2 (coarse, learned via volumetric vector quantization) — fused by volumetric multi-head cross-attention. extracted_data.title: Renal Cortex, Medulla and Pelvicaliceal System Segmentation on Arterial Phase CT Images with Random Patch-based Networks
extracted_data.architecture: 3D U-Net backbone with RPFN (Random Patch Network Fusion) coarse-to-fine: 3D kidney detector + random patch renal-structure segmentor with majority-vote fusion
extracted_data.architecture_details: Two-stage: (1) 3D U-Net kidney detector with Multi-Sourced Dice Loss producing coarse mask and random-shifted local FOV boxes; (2) 3D U-Net segmentor (encoder-decoder, 4 levels, two 3x3x3 convs + ReLU + 2x2x2 max-pool, transpose-conv decoder, 1x1x1 output) trained on random patches at original resolution; predictions fused by majority vote per voxel. Instance normalization, batch size 1, ADAM, lr 0.001 (÷10 every 10 epochs after 50), max 50 patches, 5-fold CV, 20 external test scans.
extracted_data.loss_function: Multi-Sourced Dice Loss (MSDL) for detector; Dice loss for single-class segmentor
extracted_data.preprocessing: HU clipping to soft-tissue window [-175,250], normalization, spline-interpolation resampling; detector input 168x168x64, intensity 0-1
extracted_data.postprocessing: Majority-vote (statistical) label fusion of overlapping random patch predictions; out-of-image voters ignored
datasets: 45 clinically-acquired arterial phase abdominal CT scans (90 kidneys), Vanderbilt ImageVU; healthy adults 18-50 (ICD-9/10 filtered from 2000 retrieved)
extracted_data.dataset_size: 45 patients / 90 kidneys (5-fold CV on 25 scans + 20 external test scans per evaluation)
comparison_methods: 3D U-Net Hierarchy (Roth et al. multi-scale pyramid)
extracted_data.limitations: Limited FOV; weak boundary between medulla and pelvicalyceal system; small structures (calyx, pelvis) undersegmented; trained/evaluated only on healthy normal kidneys
extracted_data.future_work: Test on subjects with pathological renal conditions; refine small-structure segmentation

D1.justification: Institutional ImageVU (Vanderbilt) cohort, de-identified under IRB but no public release; annotations not shared.

D2.justification: No code availability statement anywhere in the text.

D3.justification: 5-fold CV plus 20-case held-out test set with per-fold variance, but no random seeds and fold/split description partly inconsistent.

D4.justification: Standard Dice per structure with mean±SD and paired t-tests.

D5.justification: NVIDIA Titan X 12GB, CUDA 9.0 explicitly stated.

M1.justification: RPFN pipeline (MSDL-trained kidney detector → randomly shifted high-res patches → majority-vote fusion) clearly described with architecture and preprocessing; some loss formulas unresolved.

M2.justification: Two relevant baselines (low-res 3D U-Net; hierarchical 3D FCN, Roth et al.) retrained on same data and parameters.

M3.justification: LR 0.001 (×0.1 every 10 epochs after 50), batch 1, ADAM + momentum 0.9, instance norm, 168×168×64 input, ≤50 patches all reported.

M4.justification: Baseline ladder (whole-volume → hierarchy → RPFN) partially ablates the coarse-to-fine design, but no ablation of RPFN internals (patch count, random shift, fusion rule).

M5.justification: Paired t-tests (p<0.001), mean±SD for all three structures, variance across 5 folds, averaged loss curves.

C1.justification: 20 'external' tests are held-out cases from the same single-center ImageVU cohort; no external institution or scanner validation.

C2.justification: Single trained interpreter made GT under expert supervision; no reader study or algorithm-vs-clinician comparison.

C3.justification: No clinical metrics or outcomes; Dice only.

C4.justification: No training or inference times reported.

C5.justification: No workflow integration discussion beyond generic clinical-translation appeal.

extracted_data.postprocessing: Per-patient model selection: lowest validation Dice+CE loss among 50 epoch checkpoints; no other postprocessing visible
datasets: Samsung Medical Center prostate cancer RT patients (single center, IRB 2019-09-119-002)

extracted_data.loss_function: Per method: BCE (DMLu); categorical CE + BCE (DMLo); Dice loss (2DS); weighted categorical CE (DMmc); soft-Dice (2DRnx); Generalized Wasserstein Dice + DRO (WASS); per-pathway CE + soft-Dice (UNWM)

extracted_data.postprocessing: Connected-component keeping two largest lungs (DMLu); averaging of fold/foundation ensembles; argmax/0.5 thresholding; lung-mask masking of lesion outputs; two-step cascade masking (DMmc, 2DRnx, InfNet); majority voting across all methods (MAJ)

extracted_data.title: Differential-UMamba: Rethinking Tumor Segmentation Under Limited Data Scenarios
extracted_data.architecture: Diff-UMamba: UMamba-Bot (UNet + Mamba SSM bottleneck) + Noise Reduction Module (NRM)
extracted_data.architecture_details: 3D nnUNet-based; two mamba blocks: M1 in bottleneck extracts features m1; M2 estimates noise from learnable weighted sum of downsampled encoder outputs e1-e5 (1x1x1 conv + ReLU + adaptive avg pool, trainable lambdas); denoised bottleneck m_hat = m1 - m2 (differential transformer-inspired signal differencing); residual blocks (conv+IN+LeakyReLU), mamba blocks (dual-path linear/SiLU/SSM with hadamard combine); NRM adds ~2% params; recommends for small datasets (<800 volumes)
extracted_data.loss_function: Unweighted sum of Dice loss + cross-entropy loss, SGD (nnUNet framework), 1000 epochs (internal dataset)
extracted_data.preprocessing: nnUNet automatic preprocessing/config; internal GTV: rigid registration of planning CT to CBCT (gradient descent), contours propagated via registration transform (r-CT contour) and used as prior input channel (pipeline adopted from OAR CBCT method, Ma et al. 2022); GTV labels via HU threshold [-400,+175] + manual adjustment; BraTS: 4 MRI modalities; MSD/AIIB23: single CT volume
datasets: Internal NSCLC CBCT/planning CT (82 patients, 564 scans, GTV)
extracted_data.dataset_size: ~2200+ volumes total; CT subsets: 63 + 281 + 120 HRCT + 564 internal scans; BraTS-21 1251 MRI for data-fraction ablation

other_metrics.gains: 1-3% IoU over UMamba-Bot on MSD/AIIB23; 4-5% DSC over baseline on CBCT GTV; ablation confirms e1/e2 (shallow encoder) most important
other_metrics.significance: paired t-test p<0.05 vs baselines at 32% BraTS fraction

extracted_data.limitations: NRM only in bottleneck (encoder-level integration computationally prohibitive at high-res); benefit diminishes on large datasets (UMamba-Bot/Enc outperform at 64-80% BraTS); not significant at all small-data fractions (16%, 48% multimodal); gains partially from r-CT contour prior (adopted, not novel); limited to 3D; BraTS MRI included despite CT focus
extracted_data.future_work: NRM integration into each encoder layer (UMamba-Enc style); dynamic/threshold-activated NRM; extension to 2D and non-medical domains; larger selectively-regularized models for small data
